quiz.q: Why did traditional comparative methods prove inadequate for studying newly independent non-Western nations after World War II?
options: Non-Western states completely lacked written constitutions and formal institutional frameworks after achieving independence.
Non-Western states had formal constitutions on paper, but lacked actual constitutionalism and adherence in practice.
Non-Western political systems functioned in complete isolation without any social or cultural environmental interactions.
Non-Western nations possessed identical cultural and economic structures to Western industrialized democracies.
quiz.why: The notes explain that in post-colonial states, constitutions existed without constitutionalism, creating a gap between theory and practice that formal legal studies could not explain.

quiz.q: According to David Easton, what distinct function separates the political system from other subsystems in society?
options: Authoritatively allocating values through decisions and policies that are legally binding on society.
Eliminating all social conflict by maintaining absolute harmony among competing economic classes.
Aggregating private interests into legislative proposals through formal political party competition.
Drafting static constitutional rules to regulate the internal hierarchy of social institutions.
quiz.why: Easton defined the political system by its unique function of making authoritative allocations of values through legally binding decisions.

quiz.q: Why do Marxist scholars criticize David Easton's input-output model as status quoist?
options: It focuses exclusively on primitive kinship networks rather than modern industrialized state machinery.
It overemphasizes revolutionary class struggles while ignoring institutional stability and legal procedures.
It rejects scientific behavioral methods in favor of subjective, value-laden traditional philosophy.
It assumes smooth equilibrium through feedback loops, leaving no room for revolution or protest.
quiz.why: Marxists argue that the model portrays politics as an equilibrating machine, ignoring intense conflict, social protests, and revolutionary changes.

quiz.q: According to Almond and Powell, why can the structural-functional framework effectively compare both advanced and developing societies?
options: Both societies have identical institutional structures that perform entirely different political functions.
Developing societies only perform output functions, whereas advanced societies perform only input functions.
All political systems perform the same essential functions, even though the performing structures differ widely.
Both societies have completely eliminated traditional kinship networks in favor of modern political parties.
quiz.why: Almond adopted functionalism to argue that while structures vary across developmental stages, all political systems perform universal survival functions.
